item.text:
**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning yes. Tinubu’s 2024 posture was clearly stabilization-oriented and technocratic at the macro level, but the year still ended with very high inflation, severe household pain, food insecurity, and some fiscal-opacity concerns.

**Evidence For**
- **Nigeria: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Nigeria** | IMF | 2024-05-09 | [link](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/08/nigeria-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-staff-statement-and-548726) | IMF said the administration advanced fuel-subsidy removal, unified FX windows, set up a fiscal/tax reform committee, and used palliatives to soften the shock. It framed the package as restoring macroeconomic stability and improving monetary/exchange-rate frameworks. | `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **President Tinubu Establishes Comprehensive Economic Coordination and Planning System for Nigeria** | State House | 2024-03-27 | [link](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/) | Tinubu created PECC/EET structures centered on the finance minister and CBN governor, which is strong evidence of coordinating macro policy through technocrats rather than ad hoc patronage. | `5B.3`, `5B.2`
- **Turning The Corner: Nigeria’s Ongoing Path of Economic Reforms** | World Bank | 2024-06-13 | [link](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/06/13/turning-the-corner-nigeria-ongoing-path-of-economic-reforms) | The World Bank said FX supply improved, the official/parallel rate gap narrowed, and the fuel subsidy was being phased out, all of which support monetary credibility and investment conditions. It also said inflation and living-cost pain remained severe. | `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **Staying the Course on Reforms: Progress Amidst Challenges** | World Bank | 2024-10-17 | [link](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/17/nigeria-staying-the-course-on-reforms-progress-amidst-challenges) | The Bank reported improved macro stability, fiscal health, and foreign-exchange reserves, plus a narrowing fiscal deficit. It simultaneously warned that inflation stayed high and households and businesses still faced short-term pain. | `5B.3`
- **President Tinubu directs reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement** | State House | 2024-06-15 | [link](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/) | Tinubu explicitly pushed procurement reform and transparency, which is direct positive evidence for fiscal responsibility and against careless rent extraction. | `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **President Tinubu: Live Up To Your Expectation As Public Trust For Accountability** | State House | 2024-07-06 | [link](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-live-up-to-your-expectation-as-public-trust-for-accountability/) | Tinubu framed public institutions as a public trust and said merit and accountability should be rewarded. That is supportive rhetoric for long-term investment conditions and disciplined public finance. | `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **President Tinubu appoints new Director-General of the Bureau of Public Enterprises** | State House | 2024-06-15 | [link](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-director-general-of-the-bureau-of-public-enterprises/) | The presidency emphasized a financial expert and chartered accountant to lead BPE, which is a direct technocratic staffing signal relevant to investment climate and reform implementation. | `5B.3`, `5B.2`
- **President Tinubu appoints management team of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund** | State House | 2024-04-05 | [link](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-management-team-of-the-nigerian-education-loan-fund/) | The team was presented as qualified professionals tasked with standing up a long-horizon social investment institution, which fits a broader sustainable-growth posture. | `5B.3`, `5B.2`, `5B.1`

**Evidence Against**
- **Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-07-31 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) | Reuters reported that subsidy removal, naira devaluation, and electricity tariff hikes pushed inflation above 34 percent and eroded incomes, showing that the reform path had not yet stabilized living conditions. | `5B.3`
- **Nigeria: cost-of-living protests and economic pain** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376) | Nationwide protests were driven by cost-of-living anger, which is strong evidence that macro policy in 2024 had not yet produced broadly acceptable stability or investment-friendly social conditions. | `5B.3`
- **Insecurity, rising costs push 31 million Nigerians into acute food shortage, study says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474) | The report that 31.8 million Nigerians were acutely short of food is strong negative evidence that the reform program had not yet secured broad-based prosperity. | `5B.3`
- **FG spent N63.6bn on military equipment in seven months - Report** | Punch | 2024-08-17 | [link](https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n63-6bn-on-military-equipment-in-seven-months-report/) | Large, weakly disclosed military-equipment spending is negative evidence for fiscal transparency and raises diversion/opportunity-cost concerns, even if it does not prove outright abuse. | `5B.3`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Tinubu reversed the core macro package or abandoned fiscal/monetary discipline.
- I also did not find proof that the reforms had already delivered durable, broad-based prosperity by the end of 2024.
- The negative side is mostly outcome-based: inflation, food insecurity, and short-term hardship, plus some transparency concerns.
